ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, there is a clock face. If we connect points $B$ and $D$ that represent 2 o'clock and 10 o'clock respectively, and extend this line to intersect the tangent line through the 8 o'clock point at point $P$, and if the length of the tangent line $PC=2$, what is the radius of the clock face?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let the center of the clock be point $O$, and connect $BC$ and $OD$,\\
From the given information,\\
Point $O$ is on $BC$, $\angle DOC=2\times 30^\circ=60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle DBC=\frac{1}{2}\angle DOC=30^\circ$,\\
$\because$ Line $PC$ is tangent to circle $O$ at point $C$,\\
$\therefore \angle BCP=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore BC=\frac{CP}{\tan 30^\circ}=\frac{2}{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}}=2\sqrt{3}$,\\
$\therefore$ The radius of the clock face is $\boxed{\sqrt{3}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a clock-face circle, with a black dot at the center, which can be denoted as O. B is marked on the circumference in the 2 o'clock direction, D is marked on the circumference in the 10 o'clock direction, and C is marked on the circumference in the 8 o'clock direction. In the figure there is a straight line passing through D and B and extending leftward to the exterior point P; there is another tangent line passing through C that intersects this extension line at P, and the problem states that PC=2. Reasoning: Let the center of the clock-face circle be O. Because the central angle corresponding to adjacent whole-hour marks is 30°, D is in the 10 o'clock direction and C is in the 8 o'clock direction, so ∠DOC=2×30°=60°. The inscribed angle ∠DBC intercepts the same arc DC, therefore ∠DBC=1/2∠DOC=30°. Also because B is in the 2 o'clock direction and C is in the 8 o'clock direction, the two points differ by 6 hours, so BC is a diameter and O is on BC. PC is the tangent to the circle at point C, so PC⊥OC; since O, C, and B are collinear, PC⊥BC. Therefore triangle BCP is right-angled at C, and ∠B=30°, PC=2. From tan30°=PC/BC, get BC=PC/tan30°=2/(√3/3)=2√3. The radius is BC/2=√3.
